terms.gloss: the director of a play, the head of the company
terms.comment: Plautus’ mock-solemn name for the head of the troupe; Lewis & Short render it “the manager”, and his imperium “the management” (Poen. 44). Traupman, Morgan–Owens and Levi–Bini have no word for a film director.

terms.gloss: the head of a theatre company
terms.comment: Classically grex is a company of actors (Plaut., Ter.: Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: 'silēteque et tacēte atque animum advortite, audīre jubet vōs imperātor' — histricus
phrases.english: ‘Be silent, hush, and pay attention: the commander bids you listen’ — the commander of the actors, that is

sources: Lewis & Short: histricus · Lewis & Short: grex
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. director (of play).
Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 22 (direttore).
Plautus checked against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (9 November 2026).
